title: Check: DNS
description: Five questions on how names resolve inside the cluster.

questions.prompt: What is the fully qualified DNS name of Service `api` in namespace `prod`?
questions.explanation: <service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local. From inside prod, `api` alone resolves thanks to the search domains.

options.text: As a static Pod on each node
As a Deployment in kube-system, fronted by a Service

questions.explanation: Which means DNS can be debugged like any other workload - logs, endpoints, restarts.

questions.prompt: Write the command that shows the CoreDNS Pods.
questions.explanation: The label is still k8s-app=kube-dns even though the implementation is CoreDNS.

questions.prompt: Where does a Pod get its nameserver from?

options.text: The kubelet writes /etc/resolv.conf pointing at the cluster DNS Service IP

questions.explanation: `dnsPolicy` controls it; ClusterFirst is the default. Look inside the Pod when DNS misbehaves.

questions.prompt: Lookups of a Service in another namespace fail from inside a Pod, but the short name works locally. Why?

options.text: The search path only covers the Pod's own namespace, so the name needs qualifying

questions.explanation: Use <service>.<namespace> across namespaces. If CoreDNS were down, nothing would resolve.
